newsitem.title: USA: N.J. Gov puts $20 mln bond question on Nov. ballot.
newsitem.headline: N.J. Gov puts $20 mln bond question on Nov. ballot.

text.p: New Jersey Gov. Christine Whitman said Monday she signed legislation placing a $20 million building demolition bond question on the November ballot.

If approved by voters, the general obligation bond proceeds would be used to tear down abandoned and dilapidated buildings in urban areas. The money would fund a revolving loan program to assist municipalities with their demolition costs.
"By providing funds to tear down these unsafe structures, we can help build up the neighborhoods around them," Whitman said at a Trenton ceremony.

At the ceremony, the governor participated in the demolition of what police said was an abandoned crack house, making the first pass at the building with a wrecking ball. That building's demolition was financed under separate legislation approved this year.
